lost_reason: Rep gave repeated discounts — prospect treated it as weakness signal and went with competitor

calls.notes: Priya is evaluating security tools post a minor breach incident. Very motivated buyer. CEO Robert Chen is fully supportive. Pain is real. First call went great — they understand the value clearly. No competitor mentioned.

Priya came back with budget pushback — said $56k is 15% above their budget. Asked if we can do $48k. We offered $51k to show goodwill. She said she will check with Robert. No real budget evidence shared.
red_flags: negotiation started at Call 2 — too early

calls.notes: Robert joined the call. He said $51k is still high and mentioned CrowdStrike is offering $44k for similar coverage. Asked us to match. We came down to $47k and added 3 months extra support. Robert said he will decide this week.
red_flags: second discount given — now at 16% below original
added value instead of holding price

calls.notes: Lost. Robert chose CrowdStrike. Priya told us off the record that Robert said our repeated discounting made him nervous — felt like we were hiding something or desperate. He trusted CrowdStrike more because they held their price.

lessons_learned: Discounting more than once signals desperation — hold price after first concession
Never discount without getting something in return — commitment, timeline, reference
Competitor pricing claims must be verified — do not react without proof
Price confidence = product confidence in buyer's mind
Adding extras instead of dropping price is better but still shows weakness if combined with discount
